topStories.headline: Marion County Voters Approve Most Levies, Reject Elgin Schools Request
topStories.dek: Tuesday's election brought mixed results for Marion County, with voters backing mental health, developmental disabilities, career center, and Ridgedale school levies while turning down Elgin Local Schools.
topStories.body:
Marion County residents headed to the polls on November 3, delivering a split verdict on a ballot heavy with local levies and one notable city charter question. Voters approved renewal levies for the county's ADAMH (Alcohol, Drug Addiction and Mental Health) board, the Marion County Board of Developmental Disabilities, the Career Center, and Ridgedale Local Schools. The Elgin Local School District's levy request, however, did not earn majority support.

Also on the Marion city ballot was a question about extending council and council-president terms from two years to four years on a staggered schedule. The Marion City Council had unanimously placed the measure before voters in June, amending earlier ballot language at the request of the board of elections to clarify the intended election date and term structure. If approved, additional council action would still have been required to implement the seat-by-seat timing.

Marion County Now reported strong turnout across the county on Election Day. Official cumulative results are posted by the Marion County Board of Elections at boe.ohio.gov/marion.

topStories.headline: Marion Man Charged with Swatting After Bomb Threat Clears City Hall During Council Meeting
topStories.dek: A 74-year-old Marion resident is facing a swatting charge after a 911 caller falsely reported two bombs at City Hall on the evening of October 27, forcing members of City Council to evacuate.
topStories.body:
Marion Police Department dispatchers received a 911 call at approximately 6:31 p.m. on October 27 from a man who claimed two bombs had been placed inside Marion City Hall. The report came in while City Council was in session, and council members were escorted out of the building while law enforcement searched the premises. No explosive devices were found.

The following day, investigators executed a search warrant at a residence in the 800 block of Woodrow Avenue and recovered the device used to place the call. Police arrested Michael Lundquist, 74, of Marion, and charged him with swatting — a crime that involves making a false emergency report to draw a large law-enforcement response. Officials said additional charges were expected and that the case remained under active investigation by the Marion Police Department.

The incident renewed local attention to the growing problem of swatting calls directed at government buildings and public officials. The Marion City Council's next regular meeting is scheduled for Monday, November 9.

topStories.headline: Ohio Magazine Names Marion One of Five Best Hometowns in the State for 2026
topStories.dek: The recognition, featured in Ohio Magazine's November/December 2026 issue, adds to a string of recent honors that have put Marion on a larger stage.
topStories.body:
Marion has been selected as one of Ohio Magazine's five Best Hometowns for 2026, joining Loveland, Marietta, Massillon, and Tiffin in the annual feature. The recognition highlights communities that stand out as great places to live, work, and visit, and Marion's selection will appear both online and in the magazine's November/December 2026 and July/August 2027 print editions.

Mayor Bill Collins cited the city's momentum in a statement posted on the city's website, noting that the award builds on Marion's 2025 Strongest Town designation and gives the community another reason to celebrate its ongoing revitalization. The city's official announcement quoted Collins as saying the outside world is taking notice of what locals already know.

The Best Hometowns honor arrives as downtown Marion continues to attract attention — including last week's Heritage Ohio Main Street Business of the Year recognition for Bucci's Italian Scratch Kitchen — and as the city pursues infrastructure upgrades and economic development initiatives. Ohio Magazine's full feature on Marion is available at ohiomagazine.com.

moreNews.headline: Caledonia Man Dies in Single-Vehicle Crash on Township Road 10
moreNews.body: The Ohio State Highway Patrol is investigating the death of James R. Schilling III, 41, of Caledonia, who died on October 30 after his pickup truck struck a tree and overturned on Township Road 10 in Marion County. The crash is being investigated by OSHP's Marion post. As of this week the investigation remains open.

moreNews.headline: Marion City Hall Closes Wednesday for Veterans Day
moreNews.body: Mayor Bill Collins announced on November 2 that some City of Marion departments will be closed on Wednesday, November 11, in observance of Veterans Day, while others will operate on their normal schedule. Residents with time-sensitive business are encouraged to contact their department in advance to confirm hours.

moreNews.headline: Marion City Council Meets November 9; Committee Session Set for November 16
moreNews.body: Marion City Council holds its next regular meeting on Monday, November 9. A city committee meeting is scheduled for Monday, November 16. The November 10 Parks Board meeting has been canceled, though the Airport Commission and City Planning Commission are both still scheduled for that Tuesday. Meeting agendas are posted at marionohio.us/AgendaCenter.
moreNews.sourceName: City of Marion, Ohio — Agenda Center
